why: The student says an all-zero row is an acceptable probability row, which is the documented misconception RowsNeedNotSumToOne. They also miss that the zeros come from integer division (0/5, 2/5 and 1/5 are all 0 in int arithmetic), since this page has outDegree 5 and is not a page without links.

concepts.why: The student says nothing about the / operator or integer division. They put the zeros down to missing links.
No claim about how counts[j] / outDegree is evaluated or what type it has.

concepts.quote: An all-zero row is fine; it just means the page has no links.
concepts.why: Says a page with no links can have an all-zero row. In fact every row must sum to 1, and a page with no links gets 1/N in every entry.
No claim about the input format or how the tallies are read.
No claim about int versus double types.
No claim about the loop body or blocks.
No claim about creating p or its default values.
Accepts a row that sums to 0 as a valid probability row. A row must be a probability distribution that sums to 1.
